raw_case_text: A 16-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia underwent matched-sibling donor transplant. Eighteen months posttransplant, off immunosuppressant, he presented with intermittent fever for 24-48 h and found to be positive for dengue NS1 antigen. He only had thrombocytopenia, without any significant complications. He was successfully managed as an in-patient with hydration, analgesics, antipyretics, and serial monitoring of blood counts for 5 days.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 16-year-old male stem cell transplant recipient presented 18 months post-transplant with intermittent fever for 24-48 hours.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Eighteen months after matched-sibling donor stem cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia (and off all immunosuppression), the patient presented with a 24-48 hour history of intermittent fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: Acute myeloid leukemia status post matched-sibling donor stem cell transplant 18 months prior (off immunosuppressants).

objective.routine_investigations: Isolated thrombocytopenia on complete blood count without other laboratory complications.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Uncomplicated dengue fever with thrombocytopenia, confirmed by positive dengue NS1 antigen test. Managed as an inpatient for 5 days with hydration, analgesics, antipyretics, and serial blood count monitoring, with complete recovery.
